learning_objective: 🎯 Realize that your health depends on the world around you! Learn how sanitation, environment, and community action prevent diseases.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It refers to the health status of a defined group of people and the actions/conditions that promote, protect, and preserve their health (e.g., access to clean water, vaccination drives).
A clean environment prevents disease. This includes safe drinking water, proper disposal of solid waste (garbage), and safe sewage treatment so water bodies are not polluted.
Diseases that spread from person to person or animal to person. Vector-borne diseases (like Dengue and Malaria spread by mosquitoes) thrive in communities with poor sanitation and stagnant water.
Understanding the 3 Rs: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. Separating biodegradable waste (kitchen scraps) from non-biodegradable waste (plastics) keeps communities clean and healthy.
Community health starts with personal responsibility. Washing hands, not littering, and participating in cleanliness drives (like Swachh Bharat) protect everyone.

fun_activity.title: 🗑️ Trash Audit
fun_activity.instructions: Look at the dustbin in your kitchen. Identify 2 things that could be composted (like vegetable peels) and 2 things that could be recycled (like cardboard boxes). You just became a waste manager!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between Personal Health (your own body) and Community Health (health of the neighborhood).
📌 Know the causes and preventive measures for common vector-borne diseases like Malaria (mosquito nets, clearing stagnant water).
📌 Explain the importance of proper sewage disposal in preventing water-borne diseases like Cholera.
quick_recap: ⭐ Health is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not just the absence of disease (WHO).
⭐ Open defecation is a major hazard to community health, leading to severe gastrointestinal diseases.
⭐ Vaccination programs (immunization) protect the entire community through 'herd immunity'.
